<div class="team-wrap">

  <!-- What is DET -->
  <div class="team-def">
    <div class="tag">DET<span class="sub">Data Engineering Team</span></div>
    <div>
      <h2>Data Engineering Team &mdash; Ifakara Health Institute</h2>
      <p>The <strong>Data Engineering Team (DET)</strong> is the unit at the Ifakara Health Institute that designs, builds and maintains the data infrastructure powering IHI's public-health portals &mdash; ingestion pipelines, ETL workflows, quality-control frameworks, and the open web tools that make the resulting datasets discoverable.</p>
      <p>PharmaScope is one of several DET-maintained data platforms in the Malaria Atlas Project family, alongside HealthScope and other in-house intelligence tools. DET works at the intersection of health-facility research, geospatial analysis, and reproducible open data.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Members -->
  <div class="team-members">

    <div class="team-member">
      <div class="avatar">CM</div>
      <div>
        <h3>Christina Mallya</h3>
        <p class="role">Data Scientist &middot; DET</p>
        <p>Leads the research design, data extraction pipeline, and analytical framework for PharmaScope. Specialises in pharmacy-sector data harmonisation, geospatial analysis of medicines access, and malaria epidemiology across Tanzania.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="team-member dark">
      <div class="avatar">KC</div>
      <div>
        <h3>Kasim Chambulilo</h3>
        <p class="role">Data Scientist &middot; DET</p>
        <p>Builds and maintains the PharmaScope portal, ETL pipelines, and interactive data visualisations. Develops the open-source infrastructure for data processing, quality assessment, and web-based mapping of accredited pharmaceutical premises.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <!-- IHI institutional context -->
  <div class="team-inst">
    <div>
      <h3>Ifakara Health Institute</h3>
      <p>The Ifakara Health Institute (IHI) is one of Africa's leading not-for-profit research organisations, headquartered in Dar es Salaam with a long-standing research campus in Ifakara. Founded in 1956, IHI conducts research to improve the health and well-being of populations across Sub-Saharan Africa &mdash; with core strengths in malaria, HIV, TB, health-systems research, and demographic surveillance.</p>
      <p>The Data Engineering Team sits within IHI's broader data-science and epidemiological modelling capability.</p>
    </div>
    <div>
      <h3>What DET produces</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>Ingestion pipelines</strong> &mdash; regulator, LMIS, HFR and survey feeds harmonised into shared canonical schemas.</li>
        <li><strong>Open datasets</strong> &mdash; standardised, versioned, and downloadable under permissive licences.</li>
        <li><strong>Data portals</strong> &mdash; HealthScope for health facilities, PharmaScope for community pharmaceutical premises, and other MAP-node intelligence tools.</li>
        <li><strong>Quality frameworks</strong> &mdash; completeness, coordinate validation, cross-source deduplication.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>

  </div>
